text: Let the domain of the function $f(x)=\log _{3}\log _{5}\left (7-\log _{2}\left (x^{2}-10x+85\right )\right )+\sin ^{-1}\left (\left |\frac{3x-7}{17-x}\right |\right )$ be $(α,β]$. Then $α+β$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $t=x^{2}-10x+85=(x-5)^{2}+60$, which is always positive.

The outer logarithm needs $\log _{5}(7-\log _{2}t)>0$, i.e. $7-\log _{2}t>1$, so $\log _{2}t<6$ and $t<64$ (this also makes $7-\log _{2}t$ positive).

$(x-5)^{2}+60<64\Rightarrow (x-5)^{2}<4\Rightarrow 3<x<7$

The $\sin ^{-1}$ term needs $\left |\dfrac{3x-7}{17-x}\right |\leq 1$ with $x\neq 17$, i.e. $(3x-7)^{2}\leq (17-x)^{2}$:

$9x^{2}-42x+49\leq x^{2}-34x+289\Rightarrow 8x^{2}-8x-240\leq 0\Rightarrow (x-6)(x+5)\leq 0\Rightarrow -5\leq x\leq 6$

The domain is $(3,7)\cap [-5,6]=(3,6]$, so $α=3$, $β=6$ and $α+β=9$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text: If $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\mathrm{e}^{(\mathrm{a}-1)x}+2\cos \mathrm{b}x+(\mathrm{c}-2)\mathrm{e}^{-x}}{x\cos x-\log _{\mathrm{e}}(1+x)}=2$, then $\mathrm{a}^{2}+\mathrm{b}^{2}+\mathrm{c}^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Expanding about $x=0$, the numerator is

$e^{(a-1)x}+2\cos bx+(c-2)e^{-x}=(c+1)+(a-c+1)x+\left (\frac{(a-1)^{2}}{2}-b^{2}+\frac{c-2}{2}\right )x^{2}+\ldots$

and the denominator is

$x\cos x-\log _{e}(1+x)=\left (x-\frac{x^{3}}{2}+\ldots \right )-\left (x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{x^{3}}{3}-\ldots \right )=\frac{x^{2}}{2}-\frac{5x^{3}}{6}+\ldots$

For a finite limit the constant and $x$ terms of the numerator must vanish: $c+1=0\Rightarrow c=-1$, and $a-c+1=0\Rightarrow a=-2$.

The limit is then

$\frac{\frac{(a-1)2}{2}-b^{2}+\frac{c-2}{2}}{\frac{1}{2}}=(a-1)^{2}-2b^{2}+(c-2)=9-2b^{2}-3=6-2b^{2}$

$6-2b^{2}=2\Rightarrow b^{2}=2$.

$a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=4+2+1=7$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text: Let $⃗{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $⃗{b}=λ\hat{j}+2\hat{k},λ\in 𝒁$ be two vectors. Let $⃗{c}=⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}$ and $⃗{d}$ be a vector of magnitude 2 in $yz$-plane. If $|⃗{c}|=\sqrt{53}$, then the maximum possible value of $(⃗{c}\cdot ⃗{d})^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We are given the vectors:

$⃗{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

$⃗{b}=λ\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$

First, find the cross product $⃗{c}=⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}$:

$⃗{c}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & λ & 2 \end{array}\right |$

Expanding this determinant gives:

$⃗{c}=\hat{i}(-2-λ)-\hat{j}(4-0)+\hat{k}(2λ-0)$

$⃗{c}=-(λ+2)\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+2λ\hat{k}$

We are given that $|⃗{c}|=\sqrt{53}$, which means $|⃗{c}|^{2}=53$:

$(λ+2)^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(2λ)^{2}=53$

$λ^{2}+4λ+4+16+4λ^{2}=53$

$5λ^{2}+4λ+20=53$

$5λ^{2}+4λ-33=0$

Factoring the quadratic equation:

$(5λ-11)(λ+3)=0$

Since $λ$ is an integer ($λ\in \mathrm{ℤ}$), we take:

$λ=-3$

Now, substituting $λ=-3$ back into $⃗{c}$:

$⃗{c}=-(-3+2)\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+2(-3)\hat{k}$

$⃗{c}=\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-6\hat{k}$

Next, consider the vector $⃗{d}$. Since $⃗{d}$ lies in the $yz$-plane, its $x$-component is zero:

$⃗{d}=y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$

The magnitude of $⃗{d}$ is given as $2$, so:

$|⃗{d}|^{2}=y^{2}+z^{2}=2^{2}=4$

Now, compute the dot product $⃗{c}\cdot ⃗{d}$:

$⃗{c}\cdot ⃗{d}=(1)(0)+(-4)(y)+(-6)(z)=-(4y+6z)$

Therefore,

$(⃗{c}\cdot ⃗{d})^{2}=(4y+6z)^{2}$

Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the terms $4y+6z$:

$(4y+6z)^{2}\leq (4^{2}+6^{2})(y^{2}+z^{2})$

$(4y+6z)^{2}\leq (16+36)(4)$

$(4y+6z)^{2}\leq 52\times 4=208$

The maximum possible value is attained when the ratio of $y$ and $z$ matches $4:6$.

Thus, the maximum possible value of $(⃗{c}\cdot ⃗{d})^{2}$ is $208$.

The correct option is Option D.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

Then $\sum\limits _{x\in \mathrm{S}}f(x)$ equals
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[x^{2}]$ jumps where $x^{2}$ crosses an integer, which in $(-2,2)$ happens at $x^{2}=1,2,3$, that is at $x=\pm 1,\pm \sqrt{2},\pm \sqrt{3}$. At each of these points $|x|\neq 0$, so $g(x)=|x|[x^{2}]$ jumps by $|x|$ there; near $x=0$, $[x^{2}]=0$, so $g$ is continuous at $0$.

$S=\{-\sqrt{3},-\sqrt{2},-1,1,\sqrt{2},\sqrt{3}\}$

With $f(x)=\min \{\sqrt{2}x,x^{2}\}$:

$f(-1)=\min \{-\sqrt{2},1\}=-\sqrt{2}$, $f(1)=\min \{\sqrt{2},1\}=1$

$f(-\sqrt{2})=\min \{-2,2\}=-2$, $f(\sqrt{2})=\min \{2,2\}=2$

$f(-\sqrt{3})=\min \{-\sqrt{6},3\}=-\sqrt{6}$, $f(\sqrt{3})=\min \{\sqrt{6},3\}=\sqrt{6}$

$\sum\limits _{x\in S}f(x)=-\sqrt{2}+1-2+2-\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{6}=1-\sqrt{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Let $f$ and $g$ be functions satisfying $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y),f(1)=7$ and $g(x+y)=g(xy),g(1)=1$, for all $x,y\in 𝐍$. If $\sum\limits _{x=1}^{\mathrm{n}}\left (\frac{f(x)}{\mathrm{g}(x)}\right )=19607$, then n is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} f(x+y)=f(x)\cdot f(y)\Rightarrow f(x)=a^{x} \\ \left (\because f(1)=7\Rightarrow a^{1}=7\right ) \end{array}$

So $f(x)=7^{x}$

Now

$g(x+y)=g(xy)(\text{put}y=1)\Rightarrow g(x+1)=g(x)$

So $g(1)=g(2)=g(3)=\ldots \ldots \ldots =g(n)=1$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Given}\sum\limits _{x=1}^{n}\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}=19607 \\ \sum\limits _{x=1}^{n}\dfrac{7^{x}}{1}=19607\Rightarrow 7\left (\dfrac{7^{n}-1}{7-1}\right )=19607 \\ 7^{n}-1=\dfrac{6}{7}\times 19607 \\ 7^{n}=16807\Rightarrow n=5 \end{array}$

text: If $X=\left [\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \\ z \end{array}\right ]$ is a solution of the system of equations $AX=B$, where $\mathrm{adj}A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 4 & 2 & 2 \\ -5 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \end{array}\right ]$ and $\mathrm{B}=\left [\begin{array}{l} 4 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{array}\right ]$, then $|x+y+z|$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a $3\times 3$ matrix, $|\mathrm{adj}A|=|A|^{2}$.

$|\mathrm{adj}A|=4(0+10)-2(-15-5)+2(10-0)=40+40+20=100$

So $|A|^{2}=100$, which gives $|A|=\pm 10$; in particular $A$ is invertible.

$X=A^{-1}B=\dfrac{1}{|A|}(\mathrm{adj}A)B=\pm \dfrac{1}{10}\left [\begin{array}{lll} 4 & 2 & 2 \\ -5 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} 4 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{array}\right ]=\pm \dfrac{1}{10}\left [\begin{array}{l} 20 \\ -10 \\ 10 \end{array}\right ]=\pm \left [\begin{array}{l} 2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]$

Thus $x+y+z=\pm 2$ and $|x+y+z|=2$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: The area of the region $\mathrm{A}=\left \{(x,y):4x^{2}+y^{2}⩽8 \right.$ and $\left. y^{2}⩽4x\right \}$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From $4x^{2}+y^{2}=8$ and $y^{2}=4x$: $4x^{2}+4x-8=0\Rightarrow x^{2}+x-2=0\Rightarrow x=1$ ($x=-2$ gives $y^{2}<0$), so the curves meet at $(1,\pm 2)$.

The region is symmetric about the x-axis. For $0\leq x\leq 1$ it is bounded by the parabola $y=2\sqrt{x}$, and for $1\leq x\leq \sqrt{2}$ by the ellipse $y=\sqrt{8-4x^{2}}=2\sqrt{2-x^{2}}$.

$A=2\left [\int\limits _{0}^{1}2\sqrt{x}dx+\int\limits _{1}^{\sqrt{2}}2\sqrt{2-x^{2}}dx\right ]=\frac{8}{3}+4\int\limits _{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{2-x^{2}}dx$

$\int\limits _{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{2-x^{2}}dx=\left [\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{2-x^{2}}+\sin ^{-1}\frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{π}{2}-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{π}{4}=\frac{π}{4}-\frac{1}{2}$

$A=\frac{8}{3}+π-2=π+\frac{2}{3}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text: Suppose $\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b},\mathrm{c}$ are in A.P. and $\mathrm{a}^{2},2\mathrm{b}^{2},\mathrm{c}^{2}$ are in G.P. If $\mathrm{a}<\mathrm{b}<\mathrm{c}$ and $\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}=1$, then $9\left (\mathrm{a}^{2}+\mathrm{b}^{2}+\mathrm{c}^{2}\right )$ is equal to $____$ .

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} a=b-d,c=b+d,\Rightarrow b=\dfrac{1}{3}\Rightarrow 4b^{4}=a^{2}c^{2} \\ 4b^{4}=[(b-d)(b+d)]^{2} \\ \dfrac{4}{81}=\left (\dfrac{1}{9}-d^{2}\right )^{2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{4}{81}=\dfrac{1}{81}-\dfrac{2d^{2}}{9}+d^{4}\Rightarrow d^{4}-\dfrac{2d^{2}}{9}-\dfrac{1}{27}=0\Rightarrow 27d^{4}-6d^{2}-1=0 \\ d^{2}=1/3\Rightarrow d=+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\text{as}\mathrm{a}<\mathrm{b}<\mathrm{c}) \\ 9\left (a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}\right )=9\left [\left (\dfrac{1}{3}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )^{2}+\left (\dfrac{1}{3}\right )^{2}+\left (\dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )^{2}\right ]=9\left [\dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{2}{3}\right ]=3+6=9 \end{array}$

text: Let [.] be the greatest integer function. If $α=\int\limits _{0}^{64}\left (x^{1/3}-\left [x^{1/3}\right ]\right )\mathrm{d}x$, then $\frac{1}{π}\int\limits _{0}^{απ}\left (\frac{\sin ^{2}θ}{\sin ^{6}θ+\cos ^{6}θ}\right )\mathrm{d}θ$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{0}^{64}x^{1/3}dx=\dfrac{3}{4}\left [x^{4/3}\right ]_{0}^{64}=\dfrac{3}{4}\cdot 256=192$

$\left [x^{1/3}\right ]$ is $0$ on $[0,1)$, $1$ on $[1,8)$, $2$ on $[8,27)$ and $3$ on $[27,64)$, so

$\int\limits _{0}^{64}\left [x^{1/3}\right ]dx=1(7)+2(19)+3(37)=7+38+111=156$

Hence $α=192-156=36$.

The integrand $g(θ)=\dfrac{\sin ^{2}θ}{\sin ^{6}θ+\cos ^{6}θ}$ has period $π$ and $g(π-θ)=g(θ)$, so

$E=\dfrac{1}{π}\int\limits _{0}^{36π}g(θ)dθ=\dfrac{36}{π}\int\limits _{0}^{π}g(θ)dθ=\dfrac{72}{π}J,J=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\dfrac{\sin ^{2}θ}{\sin ^{6}θ+\cos ^{6}θ}dθ$

Replacing $θ$ by $\dfrac{π}{2}-θ$ gives $J=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\dfrac{\cos ^{2}θ}{\sin ^{6}θ+\cos ^{6}θ}dθ$; adding the two forms,

$2J=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\dfrac{dθ}{\sin ^{6}θ+\cos ^{6}θ}=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\dfrac{\sec ^{6}θ}{\tan ^{6}θ+1}dθ$

With $t=\tan θ$, $dt=\sec ^{2}θdθ$, $\sec ^{4}θ=\left (1+t^{2}\right )^{2}$ and $t^{6}+1=\left (t^{2}+1\right )\left (t^{4}-t^{2}+1\right )$:

$2J=\int\limits _{0}^{\infty }\dfrac{1+t^{2}}{t^{4}-t^{2}+1}dt=\int\limits _{0}^{\infty }\dfrac{1+\frac{1}{t^{2}}}{\left (t-\frac{1}{t}\right )^{2}+1}dt$

With $u=t-\dfrac{1}{t}$, $u$ runs from $-\infty$ to $\infty$, so $2J=\int\limits _{-\infty }^{\infty }\dfrac{du}{u^{2}+1}=π$ and $J=\dfrac{π}{2}$.

$E=\dfrac{72}{π}\cdot \dfrac{π}{2}=36$

Hence, the answer is 36.

text: Let $\cos (α+β)=-\frac{1}{10}$ and $\sin (α-β)=\frac{3}{8}$, where $0<α<\frac{π}{3}$ and $0<β<\frac{π}{4}$. If $\tan 2α=\frac{3(1-r\sqrt{5})}{\sqrt{11}(s+\sqrt{5})},r,s\in N$, then $r+s$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \tan 2α=\tan [(α+β)+(α-β)] \\ \tan 2α=\dfrac{\tan (α+β)+\tan (α-β)}{1-\tan (α+β)\cdot \tan (α-β)} \\ \tan 2α=\dfrac{\left (-\sqrt{99}+\frac{3}{\sqrt{55}}\right )}{1-(\sqrt{99})\left (\frac{3}{\sqrt{55}}\right )} \\ \tan 2α=\dfrac{-3\sqrt{11}+\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}\times \sqrt{11}}}{1+\frac{9\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt{5}\times \sqrt{11}}} \\ \tan 2α=\dfrac{3(1-11\sqrt{5})}{\sqrt{11}(9+\sqrt{5})} \\ r=11,s=9 \\ r+s=20 \end{array}$

text: Let S be the set of the first 11 natural numbers. Then the number of elements in $A=\{B\subseteq S:n(B)⩾2$ and the product of all elements of $B$ is even $\}$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$S=\{1,2,\ldots ,11\}$ has 5 even numbers $(2,4,6,8,10)$ and 6 odd numbers.

The product of the elements of $B$ is even exactly when $B$ contains at least one even number.

The subsets with no even number are the $2^{6}$ subsets of the six odd numbers (the empty set included), so the subsets containing at least one even number number $2^{11}-2^{6}=2048-64=1984$.

Of these, the ones with $n(B)<2$ are the 5 singletons $\{2\},\{4\},\{6\},\{8\},\{10\}$; the empty set is already excluded.

$n(A)=1984-5=1979$

Hence, the answer is 1979.
